name: Wonderla Holidays
tagline: India's largest listed amusement-park operator with a genuine Q1 FY27 inflection (revenue +41%, footfall +33%) and a fortress net-cash balance sheet — but a Rs ~600 Cr-per-park, 3-4-year-ramp capex model that caps it well below a 10x-in-2-3-years trajectory
business_overview: Wonderla Holidays operates amusement parks in Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad and Bhubaneswar, plus a resort ('Wonderla Resort and Isle'), and recently launched a new park in Chennai that went live in Q3 of the prior year and is now ramping up.

fundamentals_narrative: The deep read reframes the sentiment pass. FY26 was a digestion year, not just a launch year: revenue rose 13% to Rs 519 Cr but PAT fell 25% to Rs 82 Cr on Chennai launch costs and a step-up in depreciation. Q1 FY27 then accelerated hard - revenue Rs 252 Cr (+41%), EBITDA Rs 122 Cr (~48% margin including other income), PAT Rs 73 Cr (+38%), footfall 12.25 lakh (+33%) - split between mature parks (+15% revenue on 7% footfall and 8% ARPU) and Chennai's first full quarter (Rs 45 Cr revenue, 2.42 lakh footfall, Rs 21.9 Cr EBITDA, the fastest ramp in company history). Non-ticket spend per guest rose 20% to Rs 591, and management targets a 40-50% non-ticket mix versus ~30% now - a structural ARPU lever. But management explicitly cautioned that Q1 is the seasonally strongest quarter, a weak monsoon helped, and Q2 is 'much weaker' - Q1 should not be annualised. The balance sheet is a fortress: after fully deploying the Dec-2024 Rs 540 Cr QIP (Rs 790/share, ~Rs 304 Cr into Chennai) with zero deviation, the company still holds Rs 400 Cr+ net cash and can build 1-2 parks in parallel without leverage; CARE revised its outlook to Positive in Aug 2026. The earlier promoter-holding decline (69.8% -> 62.3%) is QIP dilution for growth capex, not promoter selling - no governance flag. The binding issue for the thesis is structural: each large park costs ~Rs 600 Cr and takes 3-4 years to reach 10-12 lakh footfall, mature-park organic footfall grows mid-single-digit, and the next-park pipeline is still unannounced - a 10x-in-2-3-years outcome is arithmetically implausible. The stock has already de-rated ~55% from its 2024 peak, so a P/E of ~30-37x now discounts an FY27-FY28 earnings recovery.

value_chain.theme: India discretionary / experience economy - organised leisure and family entertainment
value_chain.position: largest listed pure-play amusement-park operator in India; owns and operates parks and manufactures its own rides in-house
value_chain.bottleneck_node: large parcels of encumbrance-free urban-adjacent land plus brand and operating know-how (high barrier; few credible national operators)
value_chain.note: Organised amusement parks in India are supply-constrained - land, capital and operating know-how are all scarce, and a key peer (Imagicaaworld) has a history of financial distress. Wonderla is the clear scale leader with in-house ride manufacturing (park capex ~30-40% below imported-ride builds) and demonstrated pricing power (ARPU +7-8% annually).

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: Reported YoY: FY26 revenue +13% but PAT -25% (Chennai launch drag); Q1 FY27 revenue +41% / PAT +38% (first full Chennai quarter + weak monsoon + seasonal peak). Growth is a step function around park launches, not a smooth curve; mature-park footfall grows ~5-7%/yr.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: At ~33x trailing on a depressed FY26 base, the multiple needs a rebound to ~Rs 130-160 Cr PAT over FY27-FY28 plus a credible next-park pipeline to hold; that recovery looks achievable but is largely what the de-rated price already assumes.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Disciplined: funded Chennai + Bengaluru expansion via a Rs 540 Cr QIP (fully utilised, zero deviation per CARE) rather than leverage; holds Rs 400 Cr+ net cash; in-house ride manufacturing lowers capex; pays regular dividends; no unrelated diversification. Incremental ROCE is structurally modest given 3-4-year park ramps.
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Moving from pure ticketed rides toward a higher non-ticket mix (F&B, retail, premium experiences, resort/hospitality) and a small-format lease-based park model (Bhubaneswar) alongside large owned parks - deliberate diversification of the revenue and capex model.

four_box.note: Premiumisation (non-ticket spend +20% to Rs591/guest, targeting 40-50% mix) is a genuine structural ARPU lever; but each new park costs ~Rs600cr/3-4yr ramp with no next-park pipeline announced — arithmetically rules out tam per verdict_reasoning; in-house ride manufacturing (30-40% capex edge) + scarce organised-park supply is a real moat; stock de-rated ~55% from 2024 peak to ~30-37x P/E — valuation yes.

track_record.note: FY23-FY26 screener. Both revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% in the same FY: FY23 (ROCE 21%, but revenue was a COVID-rebound spike off a tiny FY22 base) and FY24 (rev +12.5%, ROCE 19.1%). FY25 revenue fell 5%; FY26 ROCE only 6.2% as Chennai capex + depreciation compressed returns. Pre-FY23 excluded as COVID-distorted.

quality_metrics.note: Fortress balance sheet - net cash Rs 400 Cr+ against EBITDA ~Rs 180-200 Cr - but ROCE collapsed 21%->6.2% FY23->FY26 on the ~Rs 600 Cr Chennai park build and the post-launch depreciation step-up. Trailing 3y (CFO-capex)/EBITDA deeply negative on the Chennai spend. In-house ride manufacturing keeps park capex 30-40% below imported-ride peers, but each large park needs a 3-4 year footfall ramp before it earns its cost of capital - capex_efficiency neutral, too early to judge.
